item.title: Dia de los Muertos Virtual Vigil for Migrant Deaths
item.description: In collaboration with the Immigration Law & Justice Network, we invite you to attend the annual virtual community vigil for El Día de los Muertos on Nov. 2nd at 3 pm ET. In this vigil, we honor the migrant lives that passed-on this year while trying to cross the US Southern border, which is the world’s deadliest land migration route. Share this invite within your community, register, and join us on a space of prayer, songs, and stories that immigrant names still tell.

item.title: Food Always Tells A Story
item.description: Food is so much more than just its physical elements. It tells a story about our cultural traditions, familial love, and hope for the future. item.title: With 1 million leaving the church every year, is Gen Z the faithless generation?
item.description: Gen Z, the generation born between 1997 and 2012, is a cohort of firsts and new frontiers. They are the first digital natives, meaning unlike generations before them, Gen Z was born into and only knows a world that is digital and hyperconnected. Generation Z ushered in the new face of America by being the first generation where minorities make up the majority of the U.S. population (source: U.S. Census). item.title: Early Childhood Development Ministry Evaluation Guide 101
item.description: Faith communities have a unique, divine opportunity to nurture and protect infants and toddlers — God's precious children. Unfortunately, this vital age group is often overlooked in ministry planning. This 101 guide is designed to help you evaluate how your current ministries prioritize the well-being of our youngest members (children aged 0-3) and to guide you as you take steps to build a foundation of early childhood development support in your faith community.

item.title: Our Migrant God
item.description: Mary wraps the child in cloth and lays him in a manger. When churches tell this story, we focus on the tenderness embodied in this routine act. Swaddling helps babies feel safe and secure while sleeping—mimicking the uterine embrace. So here we find Mary, building an external womb to shelter the one she cherishes. item.description: From Fear to Courage, From the Upper Room to the Streets Before Pentecost, Jesus' disciples hid in fear. After Pentecost, filled with the Holy Spirit, they boldly stepped into the streets for public witness. Today, people of faith are called to do the same.
